errorCodes.meaning: No such DID is held by this VTA, or the caller cannot reach its context.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

log.description: The DID log, present only when `includeLog` was true. Its absence means it was not asked for — never that the DID has no history.

Response.title: VTA WebVH DIDs Get — response payload

WebvhDidRecord.description: A did:webvh DID as the VTA holds it. The DID document itself is not here — it lives in the log, which `vta/webvh/dids/get` returns on request.

contextId.description: Context this DID belongs to. Deleting that context destroys this DID.

logEntryCount.description: Number of entries in the log.

mnemonic.description: The hosting server's handle for the record. Unrelated to a BIP-39 phrase; the collision of terms is historical.

nextFragmentId.description: Next `#key-{n}` fragment id to mint. Monotonic and never decremented, so a fragment is never reused for a different key.

portable.description: Whether the DID may be moved to another domain without losing its identity. Fixed at creation: a DID created non-portable cannot be made portable later, because portability is a commitment recorded in the log's first entry.

preRotationCount.description: Pre-rotation keys committed by the most recent entry. `0` means pre-rotation is disabled — a compromise of the current key is then unrecoverable by rotation, because the successor was never committed in advance.

scid.description: Self-certifying identifier: the hash committing to the log's first entry. It is what makes the DID's history tamper-evident, and it changes only when the log is re-created — never in place.

serverId.description: Id of the hosting server serving this DID's log. Empty for a serverless DID, whose location comes from the URL it was created with.

includeLog.description: Return the DID's log as well as the record. The log is the DID's whole history and can be large; it is also the only thing a verifier can check the current document against, so a consumer auditing a DID asks for it.
